heroHeadline: 25 Days to Kickoff — Iran-FIFA Hold 'Positive' Istanbul Talks But No Visa Guarantees; Zurich Summit May 20; Brazil Squad Tomorrow (Ancelotti, Neymar Fate TBD)
heroSubtitle: FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom met Iranian FA president Mehdi Taj in Istanbul on May 17 in pre-Zurich crisis talks — both sides described them as 'excellent and constructive' and Taj said FIFA 'offered solutions' to Iran's 10 raised points. But Grafstrom declined to confirm explicit US visa guarantees, and not a single Iranian player or coaching staff member has received a US visa. Iran's squad is already in Antalya, Turkey, for a training camp (warm-up friendly vs Gambia May 29) before traveling to the US. The critical FIFA-Infantino-Taj summit in Zurich is May 20 — three days away and the last formal diplomatic channel before the June 1 squad deadline and June 11 tournament opener. Tomorrow (May 18), Carlo Ancelotti unveils Brazil's final 26-man squad at the Museum of Tomorrow in Rio de Janeiro — Neymar is on the provisional list but his fate is the headline question, with Rodrygo (ACL), Militão, and Estevao already confirmed out. The squad announcement wave is in full swing: South Korea (May 16), France/Japan/Belgium (May 14–15). Germany follows May 21 (Nagelsmann), England May 22 (Tuchel at Wembley — Ben White already ruled out MCL), and USMNT May 26 (live NYC event on FOX — Pulisic, McKennie, Adams, Balogun expected). FIFA publishes all 48 final squads on June 2. Tournament ticket resale prices declining — group-stage average ~$560, 80+ matches still have official FIFA inventory. Opening match: Mexico vs South Africa at Estadio Azteca, June 11.
